newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Domos hopes U.S. will drop penalties.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Domos hopes U.S. will drop penalties.

text.p: Mexican firm Grupo Domos hopes the U.S. government will lift sanctions applied under the Helms-Burton Act because it has now cut all links with the Cuban state-owned telephone company Etecsa, a Domos director told Reuters on Tuesday.
"We hope... the U.S. State Department will be as consistent in lifting sanctions as it is in imposing them," Grupo Domos Legal Director Reginaldo Cepeda said in an interview.
"Grupo Domos has had no position on the board or management at the Cuban telephone company, Etecsa, since February or March, and neither do we have any equity stake in the company," Cepeda added.
Grupo Domos, based in the northern Mexican city of Monterrey, agreed in November 1994 to buy a 49 percent stake in Etecsa from Cuban holding company Utisa.
Domos in turn sold a 25 percent stake for $296 million to Italian firm Stet Spa in 1995.

Cepeda said Domos had since withdrawn from the agreement because financing promised by Mexican and international banks, which he preferred not to name, was not forthcoming. Domos was seeking the return of $450 million paid to Utisa, he said.

"There was a little of everything (in the withdrawal). The agreement with the Cuban government was in 1994, then the peso crisis hit Mexico and some financing deals were cancelled. After that, the Helms-Burton Act closed off international financing as a means of obtaining funds," Cepeda said.
The U.S. State Department revoked visas in 1996 for more than 30 people, including Domos directors and their wives and children.
"We believe that just as the U.S. government had the information it deemed necessary to sanction us, they should now have the information required to lift those sanctions," Cepeda said.
